title: Beyond Angkor: Ancient Hindu sanctuaries across Southeast Asia
description: Long before modern borders split the region, the Bay of Bengal served as a vibrant trade highway connecting South India with Southeast Asia through commerce, navigation, and shared faith. While monumental complexes like Angkor Wat command global attention, older Hindu sanctuaries scattered along interior river basins and overland corridors preserve early Shaivite and Vaishnavite stonecraft, Sanskrit epigraphy, and cosmological architecture. From unmortared Cham brick towers along the central Vietnamese coast to Khmer mountain shrines rising above the Mekong and Mun river basins, here are seven ancient Hindu sites across the region.
